key_insight: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA) is a model-agnostic orchestration framework that separates oncology data routing from AI inference to make clinical decision support more modular and scalable.
clinical_relevance: It could help hospitals integrate changing multimodal AI tools into cancer workflows without redesigning the whole system, while preserving a standardized interface for downstream EMR interoperability.
method: Defines LCA as a 7-tuple architecture based on Algorithmic Impermeability.
Uses an Entry Theory with Geometric Deep Learning to standardize multimodal patient data across structural and medical axes.
Routes data through a Cancer Switching Module and outputs a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP) to decouple AI models from hospital IT.
evidence_signal: A proof-of-concept tested four technical scenarios and reported negligible orchestration overhead, invariant routing during model swaps, 100% recall for targeted supplementary data requests under injected anomalies, and successful multi-protocol execution.
watch_item: The framework was evaluated as a proof of concept, so real-world clinical integration, robustness, and workflow impact still need validation.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
